method_note: AC2's ~261 cites were checked by SCRIPT, not by hand: every data row was parsed off unescaped pipes, its line cell expanded (ranges and comma lists), the doc opened at line-2..line+2, and claim tokens matched against that window. 932 of 933 rows carry a parseable cite; the 40 lowest-overlap rows in the seven moved docs were then read by hand to separate paraphrase from a wrong cite.

truths.truth: The ledger carries a non-empty run cell on every data row, records a fourth invocation naming adopt/minimalism-review/report/suggest, and holds a /cad-capture --cadence row
truths.evidence: Scripted parse of .planning/DOCS-CLAIMS.md: 937 pipe lines = 4 meta (2 headers + 2 separators) + 933 data rows, all 9 fields; empty run cells: 0; run values {1: 190, 2: 743}; empty verdict cells: 0; verdicts {accurate 849, stale 46, unverifiable 38}. Fourth invocation at DOCS-CLAIMS.md:82 `/cad-docs-verify cadence-core/workflows/{adopt,minimalism-review,report,suggest}.md` (a fifth for the three reference docs at :83). --cadence row: DOCS-CLAIMS.md:1052 `| README-78 | README.md | 124 | /cad-capture --cadence routes friction with Cadence to Cadence's own queue | accurate | accurate | 2 |`.

truths.truth: In the seven ledgered docs that moved, opening each row's cited line shows that row's claim text
truths.evidence: Scripted window scan over the 211 rows in the seven docs: 0 out-of-range cites, 134 rows >=0.8 token overlap, 43 at 0.6-0.8, 23 at 0.4-0.6, 11 <0.4. Hand-read of all 12 sub-0.5 rows whose verdict is `accurate` found every one correctly pinned (e.g. PLAN-07 -> plan.md:34-38 is the eight-key config.mjs get batch; EXECUTE-24 -> execute.md:255-258 states the ONE-round cap; NEW-PROJECT-32 -> new-project.md:300 names references/req-traceability.md) - the low scores are paraphrase, not drift. Seven rows genuinely do NOT show their claim text at the cited line: CONTEXT-06, CONTEXT-07 (context.md:163-165 is prose about dispatch cost), PLAN-12 (plan.md:86 is `<step name="route">`), VERIFY-DEEP-01 (verify-deep.md:13 is the contract pointer), VERIFY-DEEP-02 (verify-deep.md:8-11 is the bracket-read path list), EXECUTE-02 (execute.md:360-361 is SUMMARY-paragraph prose) and EXECUTE-03 (execute.md:365-366 is `<step name="summary">`). Five carry an explicit `line left at run-1 provenance` resolution and are among the 8 orphans the SUMMARY discloses; EXECUTE-02 and EXECUTE-03 carry only `corrected - 044806c + DFC-02 closed 98be3d2` and no provenance note, while the live `phase_diff` mention sits at execute.md:35.

truths.truth: The seven rows phase 4's `trace close` invalidated are re-verdicted stale with a resolution naming the rewrite, and no superseded `--event return/checkpoint` spelling survives
truths.evidence: All seven rows read verdict `stale`, resolution `corrected - 4110fde - claim rewritten to the live trace close call`, run `2`: CONTEXT-14 (DOCS-CLAIMS.md:645), EXECUTE-17 (:698), EXECUTE-18 (:699), PLAN-18 (:784), PLAN-19 (:785), VERIFY-DEEP-05 (:845), VERIFY-DEEP-12 (:852), each claim text now spelling `trace close ...`. `grep -c -- "--event return\|--event checkpoint" .planning/DOCS-CLAIMS.md` -> 0. `git log --oneline -1 4110fde` -> `refactor(4-1): convert all eight close sites to trace close`, so the cited sha is real.

truths.truth: The three head-anchored REQ_ID surfaces now state the surviving asymmetry rather than the removed limit
truths.evidence: `grep -n 2FA-01 cadence-core/references/req-traceability.md cadence-core/templates/REQUIREMENTS.md` -> req-traceability.md:50 ('the unanchored prose scan still requires a letter at the HEAD of the category, so an unbolded digit-leading id is not a token at all'), :151 ('leading with a digit (2FA-01, 3DS-02) IS admitted, counted and named in'), REQUIREMENTS.md:62-63 ('a bolded 2FA-01 IS counted by /cad-audit. Unbolded, 2FA-01 is invisible to the prose scan'). No line states a digit-leading category fails admission. `grep -rn "Known limit as of v1.4.0" cadence-core/` -> 0 hits. The stated asymmetry matches live code: planning-files.mjs:299 `REQ_ID_TOKEN = /\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,7}-\d+\b.../` (letter head) vs :324 `REQ_ID_EXACT = /^(?:(?=[A-Z0-9]{2,8}-)[A-Z0-9]*[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+|#\d+)$/` (letter anywhere).

truths.evidence: cadence-core/references/acceptance-criteria.md:248-251: 'CADENCE_PLUGIN_MANIFEST overrides that path for hermetic tests only, and only alongside CADENCE_TEST_SEAM=1: BOTH are required, and with the variable alone the override is ignored and the shipped manifest is read silently'. truths.truth: What the shipped docs claim about Cadence is true - the sweep's stale findings are corrected in the prose a user reads, not only recorded
truths.evidence: Twelve rows verdicted `stale` at run 2 carry a `divergence` resolution and are still stated falsely in shipped files (the seven `corrected - 4110fde` rows are the fixed ones). Confirmed live: README.md:56 and cadence-core/workflows/plan.md:331 say a plan review is 'advisory at solo and shipped', but cadence-core/route-table.json:52 resolves `"shipped": { "plan": "off" }` (plan.md:336 makes the same error for `diff`); cadence-core/workflows/new-project.md:60-61 and adopt.md:54-56 say a written config turns plan check on while cadence-core/templates/config.json:6 and config.schema.json:27 both default `workflow.plan_check` to false; cadence-core/references/config-catalog.md:51 publishes a `| **Risk** |||||` header with zero rows under it; recall.md:3-6 says two commands call `planning.mjs recall` while plan.md:117 and :182 make it three; METHOD.md:157-158, :309-310, :373-374 and INTERNALS.md:13 carry the retired risk floor and the same shipped-plan-gate error. SUMMARY.md's Goal check discloses this ('they are not yet all true in the docs a user reads').

gaps.name: Cited line numbers still show their claim text in the seven moved docs
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - seven rows in the seven moved docs cite a line that does not show their claim text, so AC2 does not hold literally
gaps.evidence: Scripted scan of all 211 rows in the seven docs (0 out-of-range, 134 at >=0.8 overlap) plus a hand read of every sub-0.5 `accurate` row confirmed the re-pin is otherwise sound. The seven exceptions: CONTEXT-06 and CONTEXT-07 at context.md:163-165 (dispatch-cost prose), PLAN-12 at plan.md:86 (`<step name="route">`), VERIFY-DEEP-01 at verify-deep.md:13 (contract pointer), VERIFY-DEEP-02 at verify-deep.md:8-11 (bracket-read path list), EXECUTE-02 at execute.md:360-361 and EXECUTE-03 at execute.md:365-366 (SUMMARY-step prose; the live phase_diff mention is at execute.md:35). Five are the disclosed run-1 provenance orphans; EXECUTE-02/03 carry no provenance note at all, only `corrected - 044806c + DFC-02 closed 98be3d2`.
gaps.missing: Either re-pin EXECUTE-02 and EXECUTE-03 to execute.md:35 (or wherever the corrected phase_diff prose now lives) or give them the same `line left at run-1 provenance` resolution the other orphans carry; and state in `## Reading this ledger` that a `corrected`/orphan row's cite is provenance rather than a live cite, so criterion 1's 'no row cites a line that has moved' reads against a rule instead of an exception. Separately, CONFIG-REVIEW-13 cites `38-39, 200-205` in an 87-line file that is byte-identical to a6b8931, so its second cite was already wrong in run 1 and survived the sweep.

gaps.name: Twelve stale claims the sweep found are still stated falsely in shipped docs
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the phase goal is that what Cadence claims about itself is TRUE; the sweep measured and dated the claims but twelve of them remain false in the prose a user reads
gaps.evidence: route-table.json:52 resolves `plan: off` at `shipped` while README.md:56 and cadence-core/workflows/plan.md:331 say advisory (and :336 the same for `diff`); templates/config.json:6 and config.schema.json:27 default workflow.plan_check to false while new-project.md:60-61 and adopt.md:54-56 say a written config turns it on; config-catalog.md:51 ships a `**Risk**` category header with zero rows and no risk* key behind it; recall.md:3-6 says two callers where plan.md:117 and :182 make three; METHOD.md:157-158, :309-310, :373-374 and INTERNALS.md:13 carry the retired risk floor and the shipped-gate error. Each has a dated `stale` + `divergence` ledger row beside it.
